oauth.title: OAuth Providers
oauth.bothRegistered: Both GitLab and GitHub are registered. IVE only supports one per type.
oauth.howTo: How to register (please read if this is your first time)
oauth.howToIntro: For each provider (GitLab/GitHub/Slack), create an app to get a Client ID/Secret, then register IVE's Redirect URL in that app to wire up login. Follow "GitLab/GitHub setup order" below for git, and "Slack setup order" for Slack (Slack needs extra setup for its bot).
oauth.redirectBaseDesc: When you run behind a reverse proxy or on an external domain, the server cannot automatically know the public origin of the callback URL. Save your service's public address (e.g., https://ive.dazzleat.link) under Admin → System Settings → OAuth Callback → Redirect Base URL first. If left empty, it will try to auto-detect via X-Forwarded-* headers, which may fail depending on your proxy setup.
oauth.redirectBaseMissing: Not set — the callback URL below falls back to the browser address ({value}).
oauth.orderStep1: Save System Settings → OAuth Callback → Redirect Base URL first (see box above)
oauth.orderStep2: Click [Add new] → in the modal, enter the ID first (e.g., gitlab-com, gh-main)
oauth.orderStep3: Copy the callback URL shown at the bottom of the modal
oauth.orderStep4Line: Open GitLab/GitHub in a new tab → register OAuth Application
oauth.orderStep4Paste: Paste the URL from step 2 into the Redirect URI (Authorization callback URL on GitHub)
oauth.orderStep4Scopes: GitLab scopes: check read_user, api / check Confidential
oauth.orderStep4Save: After saving, copy Application ID (= Client ID) and Secret (= Client Secret)
oauth.orderStep5: Return to the IVE modal and enter Client ID / Client Secret → Save
oauth.orderStep6: Once saved, the provider's login button appears at the bottom of the login page
oauth.note1: Client ID/Secret are the credentials of the 'app' you created on the provider (GitLab/GitHub/Slack), not your account's username/password
oauth.note2: The login callback URL is determined by the registered ID (Slack is fixed to 'slack'). If you change the ID, update the provider's Redirect URI too
oauth.note3: Client Secret is only shown once — paste it into the IVE modal right away or store it securely
oauth.note4: For GitLab self-hosted, register separately per instance and add a matching IVE provider for each
oauth.summary1: Enter ID first → copy the callback URL below
oauth.summary2: Create an OAuth App on GitLab/GitHub and paste that URL
oauth.summary3: Enter the issued Client ID/Secret here → Save
oauth.idDesc: Alphanumeric and hyphens. Used in the callback URL. Cannot be changed after registration.

oauth.alreadyGithub: A GitHub provider is already registered

oauth.helpCredGitlab: GitLab → profile → Edit profile → Applications (or Admin Area → Applications). Creating an app issues an Application ID (= Client ID) and Secret.
oauth.helpCredGithub: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App issues the Client ID and Secret.
oauth.helpCredSlack: api.slack.com/apps → pick your app → Basic Information → App Credentials. Copy the Client ID and Secret.
oauth.helpRedirectGitlab: ↑ Register this URL as the GitLab app’s Redirect URI (scopes: read_user, api).
oauth.helpRedirectGithub: ↑ Register this URL as the OAuth App's 'Authorization callback URL'.
oauth.helpRedirectSlack: ↑ Add this URL under the Slack app’s OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs, and enable OpenID Connect (Sign in with Slack) with scopes openid, email, profile.
oauth.orderStep4Slack: Slack: create an app at {url}, then Basic Information → App Credentials (Client ID/Secret)
oauth.appNameHint: Name the app freely (e.g., IVE). Use the IVE icon below as the app icon.
oauth.slackPublicDist: To let multiple users install to their own workspaces, enable Public Distribution in the Slack app.
oauth.slackBotScopes: Bot Token Scopes (add under OAuth & Permissions)
oauth.slackBotEvent: Subscribe to the app_mention bot event under Event Subscriptions (required to receive mentions)
oauth.slackLoginScopes: Login (Sign in with Slack) User Token Scopes: openid, email, profile
oauth.slackSetupSteps:
1. api.slack.com/apps → Create New App (name: IVE / get the icon via 'Download IVE icon' in IVE's registration modal and upload it)
2. Basic Information → App Credentials: Client ID & Secret → enter in IVE's registration modal
3. OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs: add the login callback + bot install callback, then 'Save URLs'
4. OAuth & Permissions → Bot Token Scopes: app_mentions:read, chat:write, channels:history, groups:history, channels:read, groups:read, files:read, files:write, users:read
5. Event Subscriptions → enable, set Request URL (events), add app_mention under 'Subscribe to bot events'
6. (login) Sign in with Slack (OpenID Connect): User Token Scopes openid, email, profile
7. (to allow multiple workspaces) Manage Distribution → Activate Public Distribution
8. In IVE's registration modal, enter Client ID/Secret + Signing Secret → check 'Enable Sign in with Slack' → Save
oauth.slackScopePurposeTitle: What each scope enables (missing → that feature breaks)
oauth.slackScopePurposes:
app_mentions:read — receive bot mentions
chat:write — send reply messages
channels:history, groups:history — re-fetch mention/thread messages & attachments
channels:read, groups:read — read channel info
files:read — read attached images (vision/analysis)
files:write — upload agent-generated images (charts/diagrams) to the channel
users:read — match reply language to the mentioning user's locale
im:write — open a DM to send the assignee a completion alert (without it, DM alerts are impossible; only channel alerts work). If newly added, reinstall (re-authorize) the app to apply
openid, email, profile — (login) Sign in with Slack identity/email

slack.title: Slack Workspaces
slack.howToIntro: Register the two bot tokens issued by your Slack app, then mention @IVE in a channel to chat with an agent.
slack.requestUrlTitle: Request URL for Slack Event Subscriptions
slack.requestUrlHint: Enable Event Subscriptions in your Slack app, set the URL below as the Request URL, and subscribe to the app_mention event.
